author: Daniel Kahneman
quote: Make a list of factual questions to assess the reliability of the trait and think how to score the answers.
refresher: Choose job-relevant criteria and score comparable evidence for each candidate. Consistent questions and rating standards reduce the room for a memorable impression to dominate the hiring decision.

author: Daniel Kahneman
concept: Expert intuition needs a learnable environment
quote: Intuition in experts is nothing more than recognition.
refresher: A confident hunch is more trustworthy when the setting contains stable patterns and repeated practice brings useful feedback. Experience in an unpredictable setting can build confidence without building reliable expertise.

links.title: Gary Klein · When to consult your intuition

author: Tony Hsieh
concept: Validate demand with a manual service
quote: I headed down to the local shoe store, took pictures of their stock, and put them on the Website. Every time someone bought something on the site, I’d buy it from the store and ship it to them. For a big believer in technology, I couldn’t have found a more primitive way to do it.
refresher: The first version can test whether customers will actually buy before expensive infrastructure exists. Manual fulfillment is useful evidence gathering; it still needs honest promises and workable unit economics.

links.title: Paul Graham · Do things that do not scale

author: Tony Hsieh
concept: Separate a good decision from a lucky result
quote: One of the most interesting things about playing poker was learning the discipline of not confusing the right decision with the individual outcome of any single hand.
refresher: Evaluate the information, alternatives and risks available when the choice was made. One lucky win can hide a poor process, while one unlucky loss need not invalidate a sound decision.

links.title: Baron and Hershey · Outcome bias in decision evaluation

author: Tony Hsieh
concept: Optimize the customer relationship beyond one sale
quote: [Call centric suggesting competitor’s website cause they are out of stock] We’re not trying to maximise each and every transaction. Instead, we’re trying to build a lifelong relationship with each customer, one phone call at a time.
refresher: Helping a customer find a suitable alternative can sacrifice today’s transaction while earning future trust. Judge service by lasting usefulness and repeat relationships, not only immediate revenue or call speed.

links.title: Jeff Bezos · Long-term customer focus in the 1997 shareholder letter

author: Tony Hsieh
concept: Design work around progress and connection
quote: Happiness is really just about four things: perceived control, perceived progress, connectedness (number and depth of your relationships), and vision/meaning (being part of something bigger than yourself).
refresher: Hsieh offers a practical happiness framework, not an exhaustive formula. Give people meaningful choices, visible progress, supportive relationships and a purpose they can understand; related motivation research emphasizes autonomy, competence and relatedness.

links.title: Center for Self-Determination Theory · Autonomy, competence and relatedness

author: Brad Stone
concept: Early growth may require work that cannot scale
quote: “Paul was the first person to give us permission to say, It’s okay to think about things that may not scale, to break away from the mythology of Silicon Valley. We could actually think creatively around how to grow the business."
refresher: Airbnb’s founders improved individual listings and met hosts themselves. Such work can reveal the obstacles automation would otherwise reproduce; scale the solution after learning what customers actually need.

links.title: Paul Graham · Recruiting and helping early users manually

author: Brad Stone
concept: A marketplace must build both sides together
quote: The relatively few listings on the site drew few guests looking for travel accommodations, and the paucity of guests didn’t inspire potential new hosts to embrace the unorthodox concept of making their homes available to total strangers over the internet.
refresher: Guests need useful listings, while hosts need evidence of demand. Concentrating early effort in a narrow market can create enough successful matches for each side to make joining worthwhile.
